signals.title: @Iykconic: Bio says building and learning in public. I've been building something. You can call it an AI Toolkit, library, guide or even a repository.
signals.content: Bio says building and learning in public. I've been building something. You can call it an AI Toolkit, library, guide or even a repository. I'm still figuring out what to call it. One of the sections is what I call the Pentagon AI. The idea is simple. You don't need to stick to one AI. You need to know which one to use for what. ChatGPT is the sprinter. Claude is the ghostwriter. Gemini is the insider. Grok is the live wire. Copilot is the resident. I believe everyone who uses AI should have these tools at their disposal. My target has always been AI for regular people, non technical people and everyday users.

signals.title: @frontline_radar: Military AI can process intelligence and identify targets in seconds, but statistical correlation is not legal proof. A weapon may hit its a
signals.content: Military AI can process intelligence and identify targets in seconds, but statistical correlation is not legal proof. A weapon may hit its assigned coordinates precisely while the underlying target identification is wrong. The central challenge for just-war principles is therefore accountability: humans must retain meaningful scrutiny, and responsibility cannot disappear into an algorithmic recommendation or an opaque model. Read the full analysis on Frontline Radar.
